recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. Follow up in the API Incubator source, after the broken-link ownership is resolved, to ensure both bulk and interaction async pattern pages use the FHIR-39347 clarification consistently.
issue_request: FHIR-39347 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked whether repeated async status polling that receives 429 Too Many Requests also scraps the original asynchronous request, and approved wording that distinguishes Retry-After throttling from abandoning the operation and forcing a retry.
initial_application: Commit 25d162090f40d6b45a5685aeb883778d4fd5d7a8 applied the approved wording to source/async-bulk.html. It did not update source/async-bundle.html, and the R5 published async-bundle page still contains the older terminate-session wording.
additional_context: FHIR-35936 split async.html into bulk and interaction pattern pages before FHIR-39347 was applied. Later commit 270e0ceb7b029dad4ca0fc5ccf5296ff370888cd deleted source/async-bulk.html and source/async-bundle.html for R6 and changed the current core page into an informative overview that links to API Incubator copies. The current API Incubator links are broken, but FHIR-53816 and FHIR-53868 are separate Triaged unresolved issues rather than final decisions in this run.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No current core source was changed because restoring detailed 429 polling semantics to source/async.html would duplicate behavior that the current build intentionally externalizes, and the old detailed source pages are no longer in the core build.
